irac.issue: Whether the Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay can levy a tax on the sale of goods within the city limits, and if so, whether the levy of such tax on the appellant's sale of groundnuts is valid.
irac.rule: The power to tax is a legislative power and must be specifically granted by the statute. The Municipal Corporation's power to levy a tax on sales is limited to the specific grants under the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888.
irac.application: The Supreme Court applied the rule to the facts of the case and held that the Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay did not have the power to levy a tax on the sale of goods within the city limits as it was not specifically granted under the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888.
irac.conclusion: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and held that the levy of tax on the sale of groundnuts by the appellant was invalid.
